findings.note: NEW round-6 question (minor): the propagation rules make signal label keys controller-owned on member Pods and re-sync them each RI reconcile, but only TEMPLATE-label declaration is admission-rejected; nothing rejects external runtime writes to those keys on a Pod. Any actor with Pod label-write permission can inject a false signal (e.g. a drain/delete-block label) that Pod-level consumers — routers, EndpointSlice-based selectors, explicitly named as consumers — will act on until the next reconcile re-syncs. Risks row "Pod mirrors overwritten externally | Re-sync mirrors each RI reconcile" acknowledges overwrite but not the spoofing window. Ask: state the trust model (admission guard on Pod label writes for signal keys, or an explicit note that consumers must treat the RI as authoritative and the mirror as best-effort).
